title: 90 Minutes in Heaven: A True Story of Death and Life
author: Don Piper with Cecil Murphey
target_audience: Individuals coping with grief or loss
General audiences interested in stories of survival and hope
core_themes: The power of prayer and community support
Hope and inspiration in the face of pain
primary_purpose: To share Don Piper’s personal account of his near-death experience, his vision of heaven, and his subsequent journey of physical, emotional, and spiritual recovery—offering hope, comfort, and encouragement to those facing hardship or questioning faith.

structure_format.organization: Chronological narrative beginning with the car accident, followed by Don Piper’s heavenly experience and his long recovery process
features: Vivid descriptions of the near-death experience
Discussions of faith, pain, and community support
Supporting perspectives from family and friends

key_concepts_lessons: Don Piper claims to have spent 90 minutes in heaven after a fatal car crash, experiencing profound peace and the presence of loved ones.
Recovery from tragedy is a long, difficult journey often requiring faith, perseverance, and support from others.
Sharing stories of miraculous survival and faith can comfort and inspire those enduring hardship.
Community, prayer, and encouragement play crucial roles in healing.
Pain—both physical and emotional—can deepen one’s spiritual outlook and empathy toward others.
notable_features: Detailed depiction of a personal near-death experience
Integration of spiritual reflections with real-life challenges
Focus on hope, support, and recovery
Often used as a resource for those grieving or facing trauma
cultural_historical_context: Published during a period of growing public interest in near-death experiences within the United States, the book resonated especially with Christian readers seeking affirmation of the afterlife. It became part of a genre of testimonial literature framing personal trauma in the context of faith.
reception_impact: New York Times bestseller with millions of copies sold
Admired by many Christians and inspirational readers for its hopeful message
Influenced the genre of faith-based memoirs and near-death experience accounts
Subject to skepticism and critique regarding the authenticity of the near-death narrative
comparable_titles: Heaven is for Real by Todd Burpo
Proof of Heaven by Eben Alexander
To Heaven and Back by Mary C. Neal
